blocks.hero.eyebrow: Depression counseling · Louisville, KY and online
blocks.hero.subhead: When getting out of bed takes everything you have, and the things you used to enjoy feel far away, you don't have to wait until it gets worse to get help.

facts.text: In person in Middletown or online

blocks.request.heading: You don't have to feel this way alone
blocks.request.text: Request an appointment in about a minute, or call (502) 523-2970. Most people are seen the same week.
blocks.request.crisis: If you're thinking about suicide or are in crisis, call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline), or call 911.

signs.items.text: You feel flat, tired, or hopeless, and you're not sure why.
You've lost interest in things you used to enjoy.
Small tasks feel impossible, and you're falling behind.
You're sleeping too much, or not enough.
You've pulled away from people who care about you.
You've been "fine" on the outside for a long time.
You had a baby, and instead of what you expected, you feel flat, overwhelmed, or not like yourself.
Every fall and winter, your energy and mood drop, and it's hard to climb back out.

blocks.faith.heading: Faith at the center, never forced
blocks.faith.body:
Scripture has room for darkness: the Psalms are full of lament, and Elijah once asked God to let him die. Depression isn't a lack of faith. If you want it, your counselor can help you bring the heaviness, and the questions about where God is in it, into your counseling, gently and honestly.

If you'd rather leave faith out, your counselor's care is just as thorough, and they follow your lead. [How faith works at Freedom](/christian-counseling)

sections.body: Depression can show up as sadness, but also as numbness, irritability, exhaustion, or a sense that nothing matters. It isn't a character flaw, and pushing harder usually doesn't make it lift. It's real, it's common, and it's treatable.
sections.heading: It's not a lack of willpower

sections.body:
- **Depression that settles in for weeks**: low mood, loss of interest, exhaustion, trouble thinking clearly
- **Low-grade depression that's lasted for years**, so long it feels like your personality
- **Postpartum depression** after a baby, with Staci, Kasie, or Rhonda
- **Seasonal depression** that comes back with the shorter days
- **Depression after a loss or a hard season**, tied to [grief](/grief-counseling), [trauma](/trauma-counseling), or big life changes
- **"Fine on the outside"**: getting through work and family while feeling empty underneath

If mood swings include stretches of unusually high energy, little need for sleep, or racing ideas, that may be bipolar disorder, which usually needs psychiatric care. We'll help you find the right provider.
sections.heading: Kinds of depression we help with

sections.body:
Counseling for depression at Freedom is practical. Our counselors use approaches with strong research behind them, including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), behavioral activation, acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), and internal family systems (IFS). Together, you'll look at what's keeping you stuck and take small, doable steps back toward the people and things that matter to you.

Your counselor tracks progress with you along the way, so you can both see what's helping.

- **Behavioral activation:** doing small, meaningful things before you feel like it, because action often comes before motivation returns.
- **Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT):** noticing the harsh, hopeless thoughts depression brings and testing whether they're true.
- **Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT):** making room for heavy feelings while moving toward what matters to you.
- **Internal family systems (IFS):** understanding the parts of you that shut down or criticize, and why they're trying to protect you.
sections.heading: Small, steady steps back toward your life
Depression in men and boys
sections.body: In men and boys, depression often doesn't look like sadness. It can look like irritability, pulling away, working nonstop, drinking more, or losing interest in things that used to matter. Luke works with boys and men, 8 and up, and Tony works with men too.

Not necessarily. Counseling alone helps many people. For others, medication from a physician works well alongside counseling. Your counselor can talk through what makes sense and refer you for a medication evaluation if it's worth exploring. Freedom doesn't prescribe medication.
sections.heading: Will I need medication?

sections.body: Thoughts like that are more common with depression than most people realize, and they're worth talking about. Our counselors take them seriously and talk about them openly, without judgment. If you're thinking about suicide right now, call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline), or call 911.

blocks.team.heading: Counselors who work with depression

team.items.text: Teens, young adults, and men, and couples when depression is weighing on a marriage.
Women and older teens, especially when depression comes with shame or grief, including postpartum depression.
Emerging adults and adults, including depression tied to grief, trauma, or life transitions, including postpartum depression.
Boys and men, age 8 and up, working through depression and anxiety.
Children, teens, and young adults working through low mood and self-esteem.
Women and older teens working through depression, including postpartum and seasonal depression.

blocks.expect.heading: Your first session
blocks.expect.body: You don't need energy or answers to start. Your first session is mostly a conversation about what you've been experiencing and what you'd like to be different, at whatever pace feels okay. Sessions are in our Middletown office or online.
blocks.cost.body: We don't bill insurance, but you can pay with an HSA or FSA card, and we'll give you a superbill to submit for possible out-of-network reimbursement.
